questions.q:
Which term completes the series?
361, 348, 335, 322, 309, ?
questions.solution:
Each term decreases by 13. Thus the next number is 309 - 13 = 296.
**Answer: 296**

questions.q: If each letter of the word TYPING, is changed to the letter immediately preceding it in the English alphabetical order and the new group of letters thus formed is rearranged in English alphabetical order, then which letter is first to the right in the new rearranged group of letters?
questions.solution:
Moving each letter back one place gives S, X, O, H, M, F. Alphabetical order is F, H, M, O, S, X. The rightmost letter is X.
**Answer: X**

questions.q: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the given statements. Statements: All lemons are potatoes. Some lemons are papayas. Conclusions: (I) Some potatoes are papayas. (II) All papayas are potatoes.
questions.solution:
The lemons that are papayas are also potatoes. Therefore some potatoes are papayas. This does not place every papaya among potatoes; only conclusion I follows.
**Answer: Only conclusion (I) follows**

questions.q: Seven boxes A, B, C, D, E, F and G are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the same order. F is kept third from the top. Only two boxes are kept between B and G. D is kept immediately above G. Only three boxes are kept between E and A. D is kept at one of the positions below F. E is not kept at the top-most position. Which box is kept fourth firom the top?
questions.solution:
F is third from the top and D–G must be below it. Combining the B–G and E–A gaps fixes B in the fourth position.
**Answer: B**

questions.q: L, P, R, V, X, Y and Z are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Only one person sits between V and L, when counted from the right of V. Only one person sits between L and X. Only one person sits between V and Z. Only two people sit between R and X. Only one person sits between P and Z. Who sits to the immediate right and left of Y, respectively?
questions.solution:
Fix L and place V two positions to its left. Use the L–X, V–Z, R–X and P–Z gaps to fill the circle. Y has V immediately to its right and Z immediately to its left.
**Answer: V and Z**

questions.q: Given below is a statement followed by two possible reasons numbered I and Il. Read the statement carefully and decide which of the two explain(s) the event/observation/information given in the statement. Statement - The railway authorities have decided to run two holiday special trains on Tuesdays and Fridays from City A to City B firom 19th October 2023 to 5th January 2024. Reasons: (I) Flights from City A to City C are booked to capacity, and airlines are planning to increase the number of flights operating between City A and City C from August 2023. (I1) Many migrants from City B who work in city A, travel back to City B on trains from October to January for the festivals. The existing trains cannot accommodate this increase in passenger demand.
options: Neither I nor II is a possible reason.
Only I is a possible reason.
Only II is a possible reason.
Both I and II are possible reasons.
questions.solution:
Reason II directly explains extra passenger demand on the stated A–B route during the festival period. Reason I concerns flights on a different route, A–C, so it does not explain these trains.
**Answer: Only II is a possible reason.**

questions.q: KBWJ is related to MZZG in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, OXCD is related to QVFA. To which of the following options is STIX related, following the same logic?
questions.solution:
Use position-wise shifts +2, -2, +3 and -3. STIX becomes URLU.
**Answer: URLU**

questions.q: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 72 - 56 + (13 + 19) × 2 - 95 ÷ 5 + 17 = 76 (Note: Interchange should be done of the entire number and not individual digits of a given number.)
questions.solution:
Exchange 19 and 17. The expression becomes 72 - 56 + (13 + 17) × 2 - 95/5 + 19 = 16 + 60 - 19 + 19 = 76.
**Answer: 19 and 17**

questions.q: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which pair does not belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.)
questions.solution:
Three pairs move both letters forward two positions. AD → CG moves A forward two but D forward three, so it differs.
**Answer: AD-CG**

questions.q: In a certain code language, 'FEND' is coded as '9735' and *FEUD* is coded as *3769'. What is the code for *U' in the given code language?
questions.solution:
F, E and D are common to FEND and FEUD, sharing 3, 7 and 9. U corresponds to the additional digit 6.
**Answer: 6**

questions.q: Nalin starts from Point Y and drives 8 km towards North. He then takes a right turn, drives 23 km, turns right and drives 29 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 14 km. He takes a left turn, drives 21 km and stops at Point Z. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point Y again? (All turns are 90 degrees turns only unless specified)
questions.solution:
North–south distances cancel: 8 - 29 + 21 = 0. Eastward travel is 23 + 14 = 37 km. He must drive 37 km west to return to Y.
**Answer: 37 km towards the west**

questions.q: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the given statements. Statements: Some giraffes are rhinos. All rhinos are tigers. Conclusions: (I) Some tigers are giraffes. (II) All tigers are rhinos.
questions.solution:
Some giraffes are rhinos and all rhinos are tigers. Those giraffes are therefore tigers, giving some tigers are giraffes. The reverse universal statement is not guaranteed.
**Answer: Only conclusion (I) follows**

questions.q: In a certain code language, *ARGOT"is coded as *12497' and *GRAFT'is coded as ^29743', What is the code for *F" in the given code language?
questions.solution:
A, R, G and T are common to the two words and share codes 2, 4, 7 and 9. The additional letter F takes the additional code 3.
**Answer: 3**

questions.q: If + means -, - means ×, × means ÷, ÷ means +, then what will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation? 62-2÷7+14×7=?

In the following  number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying g certain mathematical operations to the first number. Which numbers should replace X and Y so that the pattern followed by the two numbers on the left side of :: is the same as that on the right side of : ? X : 125 :: 13 : Y
questions.solution:
The second number is first² + 4. Thus 11² + 4 = 125, and 13² + 4 = 173. The required pair is X = 11, Y = 173.
**Answer: X=11, Y= 173**

questions.q: Which of the following options should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? BEG, CFH, DGI, EHJ, ?
questions.solution:
Every letter advances one place in each term. EHJ is therefore followed by FIK.
**Answer: FIK**

questions.q: UPTQ is related to OJNK in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, RMQN is related to LGKH. To which of the following options is NIMJ related, following the same logic?
questions.solution:
Move every letter six places backwards. NIMJ becomes HCGD, matching the same transformation as the given examples.
**Answer: HCGD**

questions.q: Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F and G, are sitting in a row, facing north. Only five people sit between C and D. B sits third from the right end. G sits to the immediate right of C. E sits third to the right ofA. How many people sit between G and F?
questions.solution:
The row from left is C, G, A, F, B, E, D. A is the only person between G and F, so the answer is one.
**Answer: One**

questions.q: Which of the following options should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? YUS, WSQ, UQO, SOM, ?
questions.solution:
Each letter moves back two places from one term to the next. SOM is followed by QMK.
**Answer: QMK**

questions.q: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which pair does not belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.)
questions.solution:
Three pairs move both letters back two places. MS → LH does not follow that shift, so it is the odd pair.
**Answer: MS -LH**

questions.q: In the word MASTER, each consonant is changed to the letter immediately preceding it in the English alphabetical order and each vowel is changed to the letter immediately succeeding it in the English alphabetical order. How many consonants are present in the new group of letters thus formed?
questions.solution:
MASTER becomes LBRSFQ after consonants move back one place and vowels forward one. Every resulting letter is a consonant, giving six.
**Answer: Six**
